clue.text: Beauty treatment for a disappearing elite

definitions.meaning: a skin cream that soaks in and leaves no trace on the face
the cream of society, the crème de la crème, fading away

explanation.surface: A cosmetic regime aimed at an upper class that is dying out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic moisturiser that absorbs fully is named for vanishing, and an elite is figuratively the cream, so a dwindling elite is cream vanishing.

clue.text: One who makes modifications would be more suitable without publicity

indicators.note: without here means on the outside, so publicity stands at the front

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement
apter means more apt or fitting

explanation.surface: A modifier would fit better if they stayed out of the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: An adapter alters things to fit new uses, someone who modifies.

clue.text: Certain it has become complex

indicators.note: has become signals the letters are turned into something new

explanation.surface: Someone is sure a matter has grown complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means elaborate, with many interlocking parts.

clue.text: To this part of where town ends

indicators.note: part of means a stretch of letters lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: Directions to the edge of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside wHERE TOwn.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereto is a formal word meaning to this matter or document.

clue.text: Film which shows there is dancing everywhere?

parts.note: N, E, W, S are the four compass points, covering everywhere
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A movie celebrating dancing all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel is a short film of current events shown in cinemas.

clue.text: Complains, putting a note on the vehicle

indicators.note: on means one piece is attached after the other

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
PS, postscript, is a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: A motorist grumbles about a ticket stuck on the windscreen.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to grumble or find fault pettily.

clue.text: Something ugly climbed up into view

indicators.note: into places the reversed word inside the word for view

parts.note: an eye is the faculty of sight, a view

indicators.note: up in a down clue tells you to read the word for climbed bottom to top

parts.note: rose means went up

explanation.surface: An eyesore rising into sight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read bottom to top, so the word for climbed is turned before 'into' puts it within the view; 'climbed up' looks like one phrase but splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an unsightly thing that offends the eye.

clue.text: Succeeded in getting a degree?

parts.note: a phrase meaning reaching the required standard, read literally as earning a mark

explanation.definitionFit: Making the grade is an idiom for succeeding, literally achieving a grade or level.

clue.text: Things that mark time and jump in store

parts.note: the pointers on a clock face that tick off the seconds
hop means jump

explanation.surface: Clock parts and leaping in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-hand shop is a store selling used goods.

clue.text: Although no longer a player, he insists on payment

definitions.meaning: a former performer on the stage
one who demands or extorts money that is due

explanation.surface: A retired performer who now chases debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as EX-ACTOR it is a former thespian; read whole it is one who exacts, demanding payment.

clue.text: An imposter makes a call to arms

indicators.note: to here means attached next to, so one piece is joined to the other

parts.note: arms stands for war, fighting with weapons
a beck is a beckoning call, as in 'at one's beck and call'

explanation.surface: A fraud who sounds the alarm for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Perkin Warbeck was a 15th-century pretender to the English throne, claiming to be one of the princes in the Tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Perkin Warbeck is history's famous pretender, passing himself off as a lost royal prince.

clue.text: Tradesman is no longer batting with tradesman

indicators.note: with simply sets one piece alongside the other in sequence

parts.note: a cricketer dismissed is out
a fitter is a tradesman who assembles or installs things

explanation.surface: A craftsman who has been dismissed at cricket teams up with another craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman who is dismissed is OUT. An outfitter sells clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shopkeeper selling clothing and equipment, a kind of retailer.

clue.text: Points obtained either side of court make one faint

indicators.note: the compass points are placed on both flanks of the courting word

parts.note: S and N are compass points, south and north
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Scoring on both sides of a tennis court leaves a player ready to keel over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a tennis court; it is the verb meaning to romance.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to pass out or collapse, a synonym of faint as a verb.

clue.text: City of cities if it lost its capital

definitions.text: City of cities if it lost its capital

parts.words: City of cities if it lost its capital
parts.note: a city whose name, beheaded of its first letter, becomes an adjective meaning relating to towns

explanation.walkthrough: Durban is a South African port; drop its capital D and URBAN, meaning of cities, remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Durban is a large city in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, and minus its first letter it reads urban.

clue.text: Ruler given about one million for part of army

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the ruler encloses the other letters

parts.note: a regent rules in place of a monarch
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monarch's deputy is handed a million to fund the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a military unit, a permanent division of an army.

clue.text: Like an egg in hotels: it makes a change

indicators.note: in places the egg-shaped word inside the hotels

parts.note: inns are hotels
ovate means egg-shaped

explanation.surface: An egg placed in hotels shakes things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to introduce something new, to bring change.

clue.text: Means of covering complaints?

parts.note: book covers, read as protective wrappers for ailments needing bandages

explanation.definitionFit: Bindings are book covers, and also bandages wrapped round wounds or ailments.

clue.text: The scientist is a very unpleasant fellow, cutting up mice

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

indicators.note: cutting up suggests chopping the mice into pieces, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty laboratory researcher dissects mice.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic is a scholar or university researcher, loosely a scientist.

clue.text: Falls for a new version of red aims

indicators.note: a new version of signals the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Falling for a reworking of left-wing goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new version of' rearranges RED AIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to be attracted to or impressed by them, like falling for them.

clue.text: A negative in time that is standing for hopeless mess

parts.note: no is a negative reply
M stands for minute, a unit of time
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A refusal at the moment stands for a desperate muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomie is a breakdown of social norms, a state of moral chaos and disorder.

clue.text: Spoil the company in turning up as an inventor

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
Co is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading the little word from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: An inventor ruins the firm by arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi pioneered radio, a famous Italian inventor.

clue.text: Something for the garden with water in the middle

definitions.text: Something for the garden with water in the middle

parts.words: Something for the garden with water in the middle
parts.note: a glass plant cover whose name contains a Scottish lake at its centre

explanation.walkthrough: A cloche is a bell-shaped glass cover for plants; LOCH, a Scottish lake, sits in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a glass or plastic cover protecting young garden plants.

clue.text: Release shortly

parts.note: a discharge from the forces, written in clipped form

explanation.definitionFit: Demob is the short form of demobilisation, a soldier's discharge from service.

clue.text: Means of cleaning sec-end-class accommodation

parts.note: B denotes second class, as printed here
a room is accommodation

explanation.surface: Something to tidy cheap lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a brush for sweeping floors clean.

clue.text: One who preserves the meat in an animal

indicators.note: in places the meat inside the animal's name

parts.note: a deer is an animal
liver is offal eaten as meat

explanation.surface: Someone saving a stag's offal from waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliverer is a rescuer or saviour, one who saves someone from harm.

clue.text: Marx on cause of death

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team

explanation.surface: A comedian who was a real killer on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a barbed spear used to kill whales, an instrument of death.

clue.text: Where animals can get across?

parts.note: read as a river crossing used by pet felines, it names a London district

explanation.walkthrough: Catford is a district of south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Catford is a place in south London whose name splits into a cat's crossing point.

clue.text: Scholarship for man of letters?

parts.note: the office of one who runs a mail office, which is also a type of college award

explanation.walkthrough: At Merton College, Oxford, scholars are called postmasters; the 'man of letters' is really a mail official.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmastership is the post of a postmaster, also the name of a Merton College scholarship.
